summary: Coburn Mountain tower, Somerset County, Maine: wooden lookout 1910, 24-foot steel tower with cab 1914, cab rebuilt after 1938 ice damage; standing without cab.

facts.design: 24-foot steel tower with a cab (1914), after a 1910 wooden tower
facts.status_note: The tower still stands, but its cab is gone (FFLA).

staffing.status: watchmen recorded around 1919-1920; later staffing not found

visit.trail_note: Two-mile trail to the summit that climbs 2,500 feet; the route is a groomed snowmobile trail that the Coburn Summit Riders club maintains. A weather event destroyed a section of the access trail, which the Forest Fire Lookout Association cleared in 2025. Land ownership and whether climbing is allowed are not stated in the sources read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Eastern US Lookouts page names the Maine Forestry District for the 1910 tower. The Maine Memory photo record calls the tower a Forest Service lookout. The story uses the 1910-era district name and does not claim a later owner.

sources.title: Forest Service lookout tower, Coburn Mountain, ca. 1920

notes_for_editor: Dates 1910, 1914 and 1938 come from the Eastern US Lookouts timeline (citing the Maine Historical Society photo inventory and state reports) and the Maine Memory record; neither original report was opened. The brief's 24-foot height is confirmed (converted to 7.3 m). The cab's removal date is not found; the FFLA legend is the only basis for 'cab gone'. Access is not recorded: no source states ownership or whether the tower may be climbed, and Wikipedia's 'abandoned' is a secondary description. The FFLA Maine chapter Facebook posts mention a 1938 rebuild by the Maine Forest Service and a later observation-tower conversion, but Facebook returned no text, so they are not cited. Staffing after about 1920 is not found.
